chinese_source: EXTERNAL epigraphic anchor (non-Chinese): Nalanda stone inscription of the reign of Yasovarman of Kanauj, found in the southern verandah debris of Monastery 1 (Epigraphia Indica XX, no. 2)
event: Malada, son of Yasovarman's minister Tikina ('Lord of the North'), makes a permanent endowment (aksaya-nivi) to Baladitya's temple at Nalanda funding daily distribution of rice, curds and ghee to the monks — the mahavihara is endowed and feeding a resident sangha under Kanauj's king
date_raw: Reign of Yasovarman of Kanauj; the date as read ('731' of an unspecified era) does not convert cleanly
firmness_reason: The inscription is physically in situ at Nalanda and its content is unambiguous; only its era attribution is disputed, so the window is Yasovarman's reign rather than a single year
notes: No head-count is given — a provisions anchor, not a population one. The donor's father bears the Turkic title Tikina (tegin), a nice datum for Nalanda's Central Asian connections in the 8th century.
references: Hirananda Sastri, Epigraphia Indica XX (1929-30), pp. 37-46
Bhagwant Sahai, The Inscriptions of Bihar (1983)
